cases.description: Smallest valid package.
Entries whose name starts with "." are not part of the package and do not change its digest.
A level-two heading inside a fenced code block in log.md is code, not a date heading: no C004.
moca.json with a byte that is not valid UTF-8 is M001; it is not read with a replacement character.
moca.json that repeats a member name is M001 (I-JSON, RFC 7493): Readers must not disagree on which id it declares.
Only entries under the attestations/ directory are left out of the digest. A top-level file named attestations is ordinary content and is digested.
The same package as a .zip archive has the same digest as the directory.
Package spec §6.4: digest lines are sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of each NFC path before %, CR and LF are percent-encoded. Paths here hold %, #, !, CR and LF.
A target that does not exist is T001.
A target that exists but has no moca.json at its root is T002, reported separately from T001.
An archive with more entries than the entry limit is rejected before any entry is read (T003).
An archive with more uncompressed bytes than the byte limit is rejected (T003).
Contract §3: the entry limit applies to directories too, not only archives.
Contract §3: an entry name with bytes outside ASCII and without the UTF-8 flag is rejected, not guessed.
An entry name with an empty segment (a//b) is rejected.
An entry name with a "." segment is rejected.
An entry name containing NUL is rejected.
Only stored and deflated entries are read; an entry compressed any other way is unreadable.
Contract §3: a stored (uncompressed) entry is checked like a deflated one. Its bytes must be exactly its declared size and match its CRC-32, or it is unreadable.
Two entries with one name collide.
An entry whose Unix mode is a symbolic link is not a regular file.
A path may hold any code point, including the noncharacter U+FFFE: the package is valid, and every Reader reads it without failing and computes the same digest.
Two paths equal after NFC normalisation (café.md, composed and decomposed): a package error.
Two paths equal after lower-casing (Hello.md, hello.md): a package error.
Lower-casing is the simple mapping per code point: İ (U+0130) becomes i, so İ.md and i.md collide.
İ.md and i̇.md (i + U+0307) do not collide: simple lower-casing maps İ to i, not to i + U+0307.
Locale variants are representations of one node; a dotted name that is not a declared locale is a separate node.
A moca.audience that is not a non-empty string is C005; the node is still read.
Evidence joined to OKF sources by id, with the three selector types. A TextPositionSelector on its own is not checked (contract §7): matched is absent.

Every evidence source is a text file under sources/, and every quote and position selector matches it. The position selector is not checked; the capability depends on where the evidence is, not on matching.

A quote that is not in the cited file, and a position past its end: warnings, verified false, still self-contained. The position selector past the end is not checked; the quote that is not in the file still gives C011.

Markdown and HTML sources are matched after normalisation: markup and link syntax removed, entities decoded. The quote is normalised as the source is, so a quote that keeps Markdown markup matches too; the position selector is not checked.
WebVTT captions: quotes match cue text with cue tags removed; Media Fragments time ranges match when they overlap a cue.
Publisher-signed and reviewed package, verified against the trust root.

A key is not trusted from the instant it expires (now ≥ expires), whatever the signing time: the package attestation is invalid. The host clock applies to reading. With no valid package attestation, its reviews do not make it reviewed (ADR-0017).
One second before its expiry the same key is trusted.
Without a trust root, attestations are unverifiable, never valid.

Content changed after signing: the package attestation no longer matches and the review of the changed file is outdated. A statement that names this id and version with another digest is positive evidence of tampering (A008).
Attestations §8: a host that requires a signature refuses a package with no valid package attestation (A009).
Under the same requirement, a tampered package is refused.
A signed package passes the requirement.
Package spec §4.11: a package that allows issued copies. issuedCopies is a manifest key, read with the rest of the manifest.

Attestations §7.1: an allowed issuer marked an allowed, unreviewed file. The copy's digest differs, but the publisher's attestation verifies against the rebuilt original digest, so the copy is signed and reviewed.

issuers: MOCA conformance issuer (INSECURE, published private key)

cases.description: Attestations §7.1 step 5: original is not the digest rebuilt from the copy. The attestation is invalid, and the publisher's attestation then fails against the copy's digest (A008).
Attestations §7.1 step 5: original is right, but one changedFiles hash is wrong, so the rebuilt digest differs.
Attestations §3a: changedFiles lists moca.json, which is never changed.
Attestations §3a: changedFiles lists a file whose hash in the copy equals its original.
Attestations §3a: changedFiles is empty.
Attestations §7: the publisher names the issuer, but the host's trust root does not trust its key. The signature does not verify (A002), as for any untrusted key.
Attestations §7.1 step 2: the issuer's trust-root entry has ids that do not cover the package.
Attestations §7.1 step 3: the host trusts the issuer for issued-copy, but the publisher's issuedCopies does not name it.
Attestations §7.1 step 4: the issuer changed a file outside issuedCopies.paths. With no valid issued copy, the review of that file is outdated too (A006).
Package spec §4.11: the publisher's manifest has no issuedCopies, so it allows no issued copy.
Attestations §7.1: two issued-copy attestations pass but disagree on original and changedFiles. Each is A002 and none is used.
Attestations §7.1: the issuer marked a reviewed file. The copy is signed, the review of the changed file is not outdated and never counts, and the copy is not reviewed.

issuers: MOCA conformance issuer (INSECURE, published private key)

cases.description: Attestations §7.1: a host that requires a signature accepts an issued copy whose publisher's attestation verifies against the rebuilt original digest.

issuers: MOCA conformance issuer (INSECURE, published private key)

cases.description: Without a trust root, every attestation, the issued-copy one included, is unverifiable, and the copy is read as any package.
Package spec §4.11: issuedCopies.paths may only name content/ or media/; sources/ fails the schema.
Signed with a key the trust root does not list.
A correct DSSE signature from an RSA key the trust root lists does not verify: DSSE keys are Ed25519 (attestations §5).
Attestations §5: a trusted key that is a small-order point verifies nothing. Here A and R are the identity and S is 0, which some Ed25519 libraries accept for any message.
Attestations §5: a trusted key with a small-order component verifies nothing, even when the signature passes both the cofactored and the cofactorless equation, as this one does.
Attestations §6, §7: a keyless Sigstore package attestation, verified offline against the host's sigstore.trustedRoot (a self-made test Sigstore, INSECURE), for an identity the trust root lists.
A Sigstore package attestation and a Sigstore review attestation, each from its listed identity and role.
The bundle verifies, but its identity is not one the trust root lists: invalid. Some valid Sigstore signature is never enough.
The identity is listed only for reviews, so it cannot attest a package.
Content changed after signing: the attested digest is not this package's (A008).
The transparency-log entry records another signature than the bundle's: invalid.
The certificate chains to a CA that is not in the host's trusted root: invalid.
A review signed with a key trusted only for the package role does not verify.

A key whose roles list is empty is trusted for nothing: a host disables a key by emptying its roles. The package attestation does not verify. With no valid package attestation, its reviews do not make it reviewed (ADR-0017).
An attestation that is not an in-toto envelope.
An envelope whose payloadType is not application/vnd.in-toto+json is malformed (A001), whatever its signature.
An envelope whose payload does not decode to JSON is malformed (A001).
A payload that is JSON but not an in-toto v1 Statement is malformed (A001).
A statement that repeats a member name is malformed (A001).
A well-formed envelope with no signatures does not verify (A002).
A signature with no keyid is never tried against a key, so it does not verify (A002).
A correct signature over a statement naming another version does not attest this package (A002).
An envelope with an untrusted signature and a trusted one is valid: one signature that verifies is enough, and the signer is that key's identity.
Payload and signature may be base64url (RFC 4648 §5) without padding, as DSSE allows.
A signed statement with a predicate type MOCA does not define is ignored: no diagnostic, and it attests nothing.
A review whose predicate names another package id does not count (A002).
Package spec §11 (ADR-0017): a review that says inaccurate does not make the package reviewed.
A node whose current review says inaccurate is disputed.
The latest review from each signer counts: an inaccurate review followed by an accurate one from the same key leaves the node approved.
The latest review from each signer counts.
A review in a package with no valid package attestation never makes it reviewed: the package id is only a claim.
Reviews in an unsigned package are listed, flagged packageVerified false, and the node is unverified.
A review dated after the host clock does not count (A007).
A node whose only review is dated in the future has no review.
A key whose trust-root entry lists reviewers may sign only as those reviewers; a review naming anyone else is invalid.
OKF requires frontmatter on every concept document.
Frontmatter that repeats a key is invalid (C002): YAML parsers disagree on which value wins, so none is chosen. The node is not read; the package's other nodes are.
Frontmatter that is not parseable YAML.
Package spec §5.1: only LF ends a line. A --- that follows a lone CR is not on a line of its own, so the block is never closed (C002).
Package spec §5.1: only LF ends a line. A --- followed by U+2028 does not close the block (C002).
OKF requires a non-empty type.
OKF requires a type that is not empty. One made only of white space (here U+FEFF and U+00A0, both white space in package spec §2) is missing (C003).
Root index.md may declare okf_version only; nested index.md has no frontmatter; log.md headings start with a date.
Package spec §5.1: reserved names are compared ASCII case-insensitively. A file named with a dotless ı (U+0131) is an ordinary concept document, not index.md.
Optional fields that break the node schema are warnings, never errors.
Evidence must name a declared source id.
Internal links that do not resolve are warnings; external links, inline code and fenced code are not checked.
Contract §11: strict mode promotes warnings to errors without changing codes. An unresolved link (C007, a warning) then makes the package invalid.
Contract §11: under strict mode a structure cycle (O005) becomes an error, but only T, P, M and C errors make a package invalid.
References that escape the package root are errors.
Absolute references (a leading slash or a drive prefix) are unsafe paths, as are references that escape the package root: they are not resolved under content/.
A malformed percent-encoding in a source resource or a link is an unsafe path, reported as a diagnostic; the Reader does not fail.
A locale variant with no default-language file.
moca.valid_until must be after moca.valid_from.
moca.json must be JSON.
id must be an absolute URI, version semver, and title is required.
Package spec §4.2: a package id never contains #, because a node identifier is the id, #, and the node path.
Package spec §7.2: a relation's version is an exact semantic version.
A package needs a content node or a member.
Unknown top-level keys are reported as info and ignored; a Reader never acts on them. x-<vendor>-<key> keys are not reported.
distribution is exposed in the package result. It changes nothing else: the package is read as if it were absent, with no diagnostic.
The distribution enum is closed: an unknown value fails the manifest schema, and the result has no distribution.
Package spec §4.6–4.8: an icon and two covers (PNG, WebP, JPEG), alt text, tags, and translations for two declared locales with translated tags and alt text. The result exposes them as declared.
Package spec §4.6: src is never a URL; the schema refuses it.
Package spec §4.6: only PNG, JPEG and WebP; an SVG type fails the schema.
Package spec §4.6: an image over maxImageBytes is M010 and left out; the package stays valid.
Package spec §4.6: an image whose file is not in the package is M010 and left out; the other image stays.
Package spec §4.6: a PNG file declared as image/jpeg does not start with the JPEG signature: M010, left out.
Package spec §4.6: alt is 1 to 250 characters; an empty alt fails the schema.
Package spec §4.6: an image dropped with M010 takes its translated alt text with it, without a further diagnostic.
Package spec §4.7: a translated alt text for an image not in images is M013 (warning) and dropped.
Package spec §4.7: a translation keyed by a tag not in locales is M011 (error); the result has no translations.
Package spec §4.7: translation keys match locales case-insensitively, A–Z only; the key is kept as declared.
Package spec §4.8: package tags are exposed as declared.
Package spec §4.8: a case-insensitive repeat is M012 (warning); the first is kept, the repeat dropped, and the package stays valid.
Package spec §4.8: an empty tag fails the schema.
Package spec §4.8: a tag may not start or end with white space.
Package spec §4.8: translated tags follow the same rules in their language; a repeat there is M012 and dropped.
Contract §11: in strict mode the M012 warning is an error, so the package is invalid and the result has no tags.
Package spec §4.9: a specific app (an https: URI) then an app type. The result exposes apps as declared; the Reader fetches nothing.
Package spec §4.9: a specific app is an https: URI; http: fails the schema, and the result has no apps.
Package spec §4.9: a relative URI is neither an https: URI nor a token: M002.
Package spec §4.9: no two entries are equal: M002.
Package spec §4.9: an app type is lower-case ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter: M002.
Package spec §4.10: readingOrder names an ordered collection in the package's own structure.ttl. The result carries the IRI.
Package spec §4.10: readingOrder names a concept, not an ordered collection. M014, and the result has no readingOrder.
Package spec §4.10: readingOrder in a package with no structure.ttl. M014, and the result has no readingOrder.
Package spec §4.10: readingOrder is an absolute IRI; a relative one fails the schema.
Package spec §4.5: a vendor key must match x-<vendor>-<key> exactly. One with a trailing newline is an unknown key (M004).
The same member twice.
validUntil must be after validFrom.
Malformed dates and OKF entries with no actor are C005 warnings; the node is still read.
Package spec §4.4: dates use ASCII digits. A date in Arabic-Indic digits is unparseable (C005) and ignored, in every Reader.
A date-time without an offset is C005; a window whose end is not after its start is C010. Neither makes the package invalid.
A validity bound or stale_after that does not parse as a date is treated as absent: it never takes a node out of force or makes it stale.
Package spec §4.4: a node's window is the intersection with the package's; a full date means 00:00Z and validUntil is exclusive; a date-time without an offset and an inverted window are ignored.
A node cannot outlast its package: at the package's validUntil, even a node whose own window runs later is out of force.
urn:moca: is not a registered URN namespace.
An unknown profile is info only and its data is preserved; a recognised one is silent.
Structure: a structure.ttl concept scheme and a node bound to a declared concept.
Structure: structure.ttl is not Turtle, so nothing is declared. Warnings only; the structured capability is withheld.
Structure: a node binds to a concept no structure file declares.
Structure: owl:imports would make a Reader fetch; it is reported, never followed.
requires forms a cycle.
A 30,000-concept requires chain, within every structure limit, reads without failing: structure traversal must not exhaust the call stack.
structure.json is an ordinary package file. No Reader checks it against structure.ttl (O004 is retired, ADR-0019).
A procedure: parts, an ordered collection of steps, and requires.
A structure file over the host's triple limit is refused (O001), and its bindings are then undeclared.
YAML aliases in frontmatter are refused (C002): alias expansion is a denial-of-service vector.
Contract §3: evidence checks are bounded per package. Past the budget, an entry is not checked and matched is absent.
Source bytes scanned for evidence are bounded per package, counted once per check.
A package written for mocaVersion 0.3: the digest is computed with moca-digest-v2, and M008 tells the host older pins will not match.
Package spec §14: a package written for a newer mocaVersion is read on a best-effort basis, and M009 says so.
Package spec §14: mocaVersion is compared numerically, so 00.03 is 0.3 and M008 applies.
A mocaVersion with a trailing newline is not major.minor: the manifest fails the schema, and there is no M008.
Only ASCII digits make a mocaVersion: one in Arabic-Indic digits fails the schema, and no Reader throws.
Schema patterns have their ECMAScript meaning in every Reader: a no-break space (U+00A0) is white space, so an id containing one fails the schema.
A composition-only package whose members resolve and match their pinned digests.
Without a resolver, members are exposed unresolved and nothing is reported.
A resolved member whose digest differs from its pin.
The resolver cannot find a member.
Members that include each other.
A package that composes another version of the same package is not a cycle: cycles are detected by id and version.
A supersedes relation in a package with no valid package attestation is reported (R004, info) and has no effect.
The same package, signed by a key whose ids cover the target's id, makes the relation with no diagnostic.
A lexical sidecar bound to the package digest.
Sidecar §5: an item's text, when present, must be exactly the package's bytes at start..end. A sidecar cannot attach other text to a node, for example to stuff keywords; it is not used (S004).
Built for a different digest.
chunkIndex is not below chunkCount.
Payload format this Reader does not know.
Bound to another package.
index.json breaks the schema: a dense index without a model.
storage.vectors holds fewer float32 rows than there are payload items: the sidecar is not usable.
The default retrieval policy: superseded, out-of-force and deprecated content is never returned; stale content is returned.
Contract §7: a library refuses a second package with the same id and version but a different digest (L001); only the first is searched.
Reader contract §7: records of an issued copy carry package.issuedCopy, and a record from a changed file has node.issuedChange.

issuers: MOCA conformance issuer (INSECURE, published private key)

cases.description: Attestations §7.1: a review of a changed file is listed with fileChanged and does not count, so the file's review status is none.
Reader contract §7: a second issued copy of the same original is noted (L002, info), not refused as a conflict (L001). Only the first is loaded.
Package spec §7.2: without a trust root nothing is signed, so the supersedes relation has no effect and the superseded version is returned.
A signer whose ids do not cover the target's id cannot make a relation take effect.
An ids entry that does not end in /, : or # matches only that exact id, never a longer one.
A host that allows unsigned relations applies them: the superseded version is left out.
Package spec §7.2: an authorised conflictsWith marks the nodes of both packages contested. Contested content is returned, flagged, never left out.
Package spec §7.2: with no trust root the conflictsWith is not authorised (the package reports R004), and neither package is contested.
With the host's opt-in, excluded content is returned, flagged.
Records outside the host's audience set are removed even when the caller includes everything.
Contract §8 (ADR-0016): under an audience set, a node with no label is outside the set, and a malformed label never matches.
A host that allows unlabelled content gets it alongside its audiences; a malformed label still never matches.
The gate applies the audience rules whatever the backend returns.
A translation with no label of its own takes its default representation's label: the French page of an internal node is internal.
A backend that ignores every filter and returns every node, plus a hit from a package that is not loaded. Search still applies the policy and drops the unknown hit.
A requested locale returns that locale's representation, or the default one for a node without it.
Package spec §5.4: a request for fr-CA falls back to fr (the request truncated, RFC 4647 Lookup).
A request for pt, with no pt representation, takes the first representation whose tag starts with pt- (here pt-BR).
Language tags compare case-insensitively.
Contract §9.2: with no locale requested, the gate keeps one result per node representation and span, so the English, French and Brazilian Portuguese pages of one node are three results.
Structure: a concept filter keeps only records bound to one of the concepts.
Dense search over sidecar vectors with the conformance embedder, whose identity matches the sidecar's model.
Dense search over the deprecated form, a JSON vector on each payload item: Readers still accept it.
The host embedder is a different model from the sidecar's: S006, and no dense search.
Contract §9.3: the host embedder has the sidecar model's name but another version: S006, and no dense search.
Contract §9.3: the host embedder has the sidecar model's name and version but another number of dimensions: S006, and no dense search.
The index and the host embedder declare the same prefixes: dense search runs.
The host embedder declares other prefixes than the index: S006, and no dense search.
Contract §9.3: the index declares prefixes and the host embedder declares none. A prefix declared on one side only is a mismatch (S006): the vectors are not searched.
Two packages; the dense sidecar binds only to one. The other has no vectors: S007, and no hits from it.
Hybrid search with the default fusion: hello.md, which has vectors, and the locales nodes, which have none and come back through the lexical side.
Hybrid search with the lexical weight 0: only the dense side counts, so only hello.md comes back.
No model.distance: cosine. Query [1,0]; a.md [1,0] scores 1, b.md [3,3] 0.71, so a.md comes first.
model.distance dot. Query [1,0]; a.md [1,0] scores 1, b.md [3,3] 3, so b.md comes first.
model.distance euclidean (negative distance). Query [1,0]; a.md [10,0] is 9 away, b.md [0.9,0.1] 0.14, so b.md comes first.
A sidecar whose items carry no text (it is optional): lexical search runs over the package text the offsets point at.
concept: preferred label, labels, definition, deprecation and layer.
Contract §10: traversal over a cycle visits each concept once and never returns the start. A requires B requires C requires A, so transitive requires of A is C, then B.
sequence: members in list order.
parts: direct parts, ordered by IRI.
requires, direct.
requiredBy, ordered by IRI.
nodes bound to a concept and its parts, ordered by node reference.
An organisation overlay adds a requirement; transitive requires lists dependencies first, and each item names the layer that stated it.
An overlay can declare new concepts under a package concept.
scope keeps only nodes bound to the concept or its descendants.
Contract §9: upTo at the first member keeps that step, and records off the reading order (a glossary, notes bound to no concept).
Contract §9: upTo at module 1. Basics sits under module 1 and module 3, and takes the first, so it passes. A node bound to module 1 and module 3 does not pass.
Contract §9: upTo at module 2 keeps a part of module 2 (dcterms:hasPart) and everything before it; module 3 does not pass.
Contract §9: upTo at the last member keeps everything.
Contract §9: upTo limits only the packages whose reading order has it as a member. A reference package loaded beside the course is not limited.
Contract §9: upTo combines with scope. scope keeps module 1 and Basics; upTo at module 1 then drops the node also bound to module 3.
Contract §9: an upTo that no loaded reading order places, neither a member nor a descendant, limits nothing, and the Reader reports S008.
Contract §9: upTo at Basics, a descendant of module 1 (and of module 3). It is placed at the first member that contains it, so it limits exactly as module 1 does.
Contract §9.2: an ingress hook that tries to remove upTo. The gate follows the caller.
Contract §9.4: a store search applies upTo from the package states, as a library search does.
The default ontology-guided hooks add the nodes of required concepts; the gate still applies.
An egress hook that returns everything, and a record from a package that is not loaded: the gate removes all that policy and audience exclude.
An ingress hook that asks for content the policy excludes, a larger limit and another locale: the gate follows the caller.
A store search resolves hits from ingest-time records and returns only packages in the host's allowlist.

Contract §9.4: a store search recomputes every library- and trust-dependent field from the host's package states. Version 1.0.0 was ingested alone, so its stored records say it is not superseded; once 2.0.0, which supersedes it, is loaded, the store search leaves it out.
Encrypted packages §2, §5.1: an envelope is recognised by its content. With no key provider, or in a Reader without the encryption feature, it is not opened (E001), and nothing inside it is exposed.
An envelope for an X25519 recipient, with the default outline (id, version, title). Opened, it is the inner archive, with the same digest.
An envelope for a passphrase (one scrypt stanza, work factor 10).
An envelope with no outline: moca-enc.json holds only the format.
An envelope with the opt-in structure copy, outline/structure.ttl, equal to the inner structure.ttl.
The package inside the envelope-large and envelope-truncated envelopes, read plain.
An envelope whose payload has more than one age chunk.
Encrypted packages §5.1: a key of a kind no stanza uses (a passphrase for an X25519 file) is E001, not E002.
An X25519 identity that is not a recipient (E002).
A wrong passphrase (E002).
A file key from the host that fails the header MAC (E002).
The payload's final chunk is missing (E003); no plaintext is used.
One payload byte changed after encryption (E003).
Encrypted packages §3: the outline's title differs from the inner manifest's (E004). Nothing inside is exposed.
The structure copy differs from the inner structure.ttl by one line (E004).
Encrypted packages §2: an entry the layout does not name (E005).
No package.age (E005).
moca-enc.json names another format (E005).
A Zip with both moca.json and moca-enc.json at its root (E005).
package.age is deflated, not stored (E005).
Encrypted packages §4: an scrypt stanza beside an X25519 stanza (E006), found before any key is used.
An scrypt work factor of 21, over the default limit of 20 (E006), refused without running scrypt.
Reader contract §3: the limits apply again to the archive inside an envelope. The envelope is small; the inner archive inflates past maxBytes (T003).
Encrypted packages §6: index.age is opened through the same key provider and bound to the package from the same envelope.
Encrypted packages §6: an index.age whose payload fails authentication is reported by the binding (E003) and is not used. The package stays valid.
Encrypted packages §2: an index.age that is deflated, not stored, makes the envelope invalid (E005).
Encrypted packages §3: an outline with translations and tags and a cover copy equal to the inner manifest's first cover. It opens.
Encrypted packages §3: a cover copy that differs by one byte from the inner cover is E004.
Encrypted packages §3: the copy's extension must match the cover's type; a WebP cover copied as outline/cover.png is E004.
Encrypted packages §3: a cover copy when the inner manifest has no cover image is E004.
Encrypted packages §2: outline/cover.gif is not an allowed entry: E005, before any key is asked for.
Encrypted packages §2: an envelope has at most one cover copy: E005.
Encrypted packages §2: a cover copy over maxImageBytes is E005, before any key is asked for.
Encrypted packages §3: an outline whose translated title differs from the decrypted manifest's is E004.
Encrypted packages §3: apps as an outline property, equal to the inner manifest's. It opens.
Encrypted packages §3: an outline whose apps differ from the decrypted manifest's (here, in another order) is E004.
